## Capture: fresh paired coordinates and first-match indexing

Keep the existing guarded query/check semantics and limits. Do not access
private champion::info/camp::info, raw detail imports or patch the SDK.

The public `vision::camps()` implementation enumerates
`vision::camp_tiles().positions()` and calls public `vision::camp_at(p)` for
each position. Replace this with a local helper returning owned pairs of that
same camp handle and its enumerated CURRENT position, inside ONE equivalent
existing query scope. Preserve exactly that enumeration/public-call order and
before/after checks. For an oversized visible list (>Limits::camps), preserve
ALL public camp_at/metadata calls and the outer postcheck before returning
incomplete, including propagation of a late metadata error. Do not early-return
or truncate the enumeration. It is sufficient to retain at most256pairs plus
an overflow flag while completing the original public calls; an overflow never
publishes a Scene. The public position enumeration remains bounded by the
supported cell count. Test an over-cap list with a late error. Reuse those
coordinates rather than call c.position()
again per camp; the current code's extra guarded getter costs5raw imports per
visible camp. Do not replace a current coordinate with spawn_position/last.

Public contract supporting equivalence: rules specify sequential camp then
champion turns and fuel exhaustion resuming NEXT ROUND; capture performs no
mutation. camp_at(p) identifies the currently visible camp at current tile p.
A completed same actor/life/round/revision capture therefore has no intervening
movement, and the enumerated positions equal later current position getters.
Rollover during enumeration/helper/metadata still stops at the existing outer
postcheck/final current(s.epoch), with no issuance from that scene. These are
public-contract obligations, not a license to assume coherent partial results.
Propagate real camp_at/metadata errors as before; no catch-to-empty fallback.
Retain actual query count for calls made; do not fake removed getter tickets.

For member matching, build a fixed bounded sorted lookup of
`(public uint32 camp handle, original visible index)` per capture, sorted by
both fields. Use lower_bound to find the FIRST original visible match, exactly
as old std::find did. Keep the ORIGINAL static-member loop, update order,
relevance/effect_groups logic, mapped count check and all per-member fresh
state/Strength checks. This preserves first-match behavior even for duplicate
or missing handles in fixtures. No new SDK query, sorted Scene order or
presumption that handles are dense/small. Do not require an undocumented
handle≤256. Source work changes from O(M*V) to O(VlogV+MlogV).

Reserve supported output sizes to avoid repeated growth; all indexes/buffers
must be bounded by existing capacities, with explicit unsupported results.
No new full-map buffer, persistent field, stale visibility cache or second
native compute. All Scene members and unknown observations remain present.
Keep state after actual action freshly observed; no cross-action scalar reuse.
